subject.title: fix(memory-core): honor private-network settings for OpenAI-compatible embeddings

question: Should memory embeddings inherit `models.providers.<id>.request.allowPrivateNetwork`, including explicit `false` disabling exact-host private trust, as the canonical trust boundary for configured OpenAI-compatible providers?
rationale: The implementation is coherent, but it changes which existing provider security setting governs memory embedding network reach and has upgrade-sensitive behavior for explicit denial.

options.title: Accept provider-policy inheritance
options.body: Treat the existing provider request policy as the canonical owner for memory embedding private-network trust and land the PR with its omitted/true/false semantics.

options.title: Keep exact-host compatibility for explicit false
options.body: Revise the branch so explicit denial blocks broad private-network access but does not break exact configured-host trust for existing memory embedding setups.

options.title: Reject coupling to provider policy
options.body: Close or pause this PR in favor of a separate memory-owned trust knob or provider API contract if memory embeddings should not inherit provider request policy.

recommendation.title: Accept provider-policy inheritance
recommendation.body: Treat the existing provider request policy as the canonical owner for memory embedding private-network trust and land the PR with its omitted/true/false semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved question is specifically about the SSRF/provider request-policy boundary, and Kaspre is the strongest visible adjacent owner from recent history.
